findings.claim: The plan says the skill follows the prototype, but the prototype judged each change in its own isolated claude -p call. The skill judges every listed change in one agent session, reading message, plan, diff and the earlier index for each, and the plan never says how it handles a long list. kmctl decision candidates --json over this repository's measured range lists 163 changes and is about 205 KB (roughly 50k tokens) before any diff or plan is read. A first run in a repo with no records, or a --since far back, is the history scan the operator asked for, and one context cannot judge that the way the measurement did. So the measured 25/30 recall and 59% precision say nothing about the skill as planned. The plan should say how a long range is judged (per-change or batched subagents where the harness has them, a count shown before judging with a prompt to narrow by --since, or both), and its skill-creator evals should include a range with known answers, e.g. the measured 14799749..ee87e883 against results/labels.json, so recall can be compared with the prototype's. Whether one session holds up is something to run, not argue: a spike can run the drafted skill on that range and compare.

Two how-to pages list kmctl's skills as 'seven skills' and name all seven: docs/how-to/install-kmctl-with-apm.md:141 and docs/how-to/install-the-plugin-and-the-ci-action.md:95 and :137. An eighth skill makes them wrong, and docs-layout's docs-describe-what-exists rule needs them fixed in the same change. Neither page is in O1's touches.
